text: For the LORD giveth wisdom: out of his mouth cometh knowledge and understanding.
reflection: We often look for wisdom in many places: books, experts, experience, and the advice of friends. These can all be helpful. But Proverbs points us to the true source: "For the LORD giveth wisdom: out of his mouth cometh knowledge and understanding." Wisdom is not something we generate on our own. It is a gift that God delights to give. And it comes from His mouth, from what He has spoken. That is why time in His Word is never wasted. When we read Scripture, we are listening to the voice that gives wisdom. As we begin this month focused on wisdom and spiritual growth, consider where you have been looking for direction. Have you been turning to God first, or last? He is not stingy with wisdom. He gives generously to those who ask. Today, open His Word and ask Him for understanding. Then listen. The God who speaks wisdom is ready to share it with you.
question: Where do you need wisdom today, and have you asked God for it through His Word?
prayer: Lord, You give wisdom, and from Your mouth come knowledge and understanding. Open Your Word to me today, and give me the understanding I need. Amen.

text: And the spirit of the LORD shall rest upon him, the spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of counsel and might, the spirit of knowledge and of the fear of the LORD…
reflection: Isaiah looked ahead to a coming King from the family of Jesse, and he described the Spirit who would rest upon Him: "the spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of counsel and might, the spirit of knowledge and of the fear of the LORD." This prophecy was fulfilled in Jesus. Every quality of perfect leadership and wisdom rested fully on Him. He always knew what to say, when to be gentle, and when to be firm. He had wisdom for the confused, counsel for the troubled, and might for the weak. And here is the wonderful news: the same Spirit who rested on Jesus now lives in those who belong to Him. We do not receive this Spirit in the same fullness as Christ, but we are not left without help. When we need wisdom, counsel, or strength, the Spirit is near. Today, ask the Holy Spirit to give you wisdom and understanding for whatever you face. You do not have to rely on your own limited insight.
question: What are you facing today that needs the Spirit's wisdom, counsel, or might?
prayer: Lord, the Spirit of wisdom and understanding, counsel and might, rested on Jesus. Let that same Spirit guide me today, so I do not rely on my own limited insight. Amen.

text: The fear of the LORD is the beginning of knowledge: but fools despise wisdom and instruction.
reflection: Proverbs opens with its foundational truth: "The fear of the LORD is the beginning of knowledge: but fools despise wisdom and instruction." Everything else in the book is built on this. To fear the Lord is to hold Him in awe, to take Him seriously, to give Him first place in your life. That reverence is where true knowledge begins. Without it, we may gather facts, but we will miss the meaning. The verse also gives a warning. Fools despise wisdom and instruction. A fool in Proverbs is not someone with a low IQ. It is someone who refuses to be taught, who thinks they already know best. Pride closes the door to learning. Humility opens it. Today, check the posture of your heart. Are you willing to be taught by God, even when it challenges your opinions? Begin with reverence. Bow before His greatness. And then open yourself to the instruction He gives. That is the beginning of a wise life.
question: Are you willing to be taught by God, even when He challenges your opinions?
prayer: Lord, You are the beginning of all true knowledge. Give me a reverent and teachable heart, open to the instruction You give. Amen.

text: That the God of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of glory, may give unto you the spirit of wisdom and revelation in the knowledge of him…
reflection: Paul's prayer for the Ephesians shows what he valued most. He did not pray first for their comfort or success. He prayed "that the God of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of glory, may give unto you the spirit of wisdom and revelation in the knowledge of him." Paul wanted them to know God more deeply. Not just to know about Him, but to know Him personally. And he recognized that this kind of knowledge requires divine help. We need the Spirit to open our eyes and reveal who God is. This is a beautiful prayer to pray for ourselves and for others. How often do we pray for the people we love to know God better? We pray for their health, jobs, and safety, all good things. But the greatest gift we could ask for them is deeper knowledge of God. Today, pray this prayer for yourself. Then pray it by name for someone you love. Ask God to reveal Himself to them.
question: Whom can you pray for by name today, asking God to reveal Himself to them?
prayer: Father of glory, give me the spirit of wisdom and revelation in the knowledge of You. Reveal Yourself to me, and to those I love, more deeply each day. Amen.

text: The fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom: and the knowledge of the holy is understanding.
reflection: This verse is close to Proverbs 1:7, but it adds something important: "The fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom: and the knowledge of the holy is understanding." Wisdom begins with reverence, and understanding grows as we come to know the Holy One. In other words, wisdom is not ultimately about techniques or tips for living. It is about a relationship. The more we know God, His character, His ways, His heart, the more we understand life. A person may be very clever and still lack understanding, because they do not know the One who made everything. And a person with little formal education may be deeply wise, because they walk closely with God. This is encouraging. Wisdom is available to anyone willing to seek the Lord. Today, spend time getting to know God better. Read about His character in Scripture. Notice His holiness and His goodness. As you know Him more, you will understand life more clearly.
question: What part of God's character could you spend time getting to know better today?
prayer: Holy One, wisdom begins with reverence for You. As I come to know Your character and Your heart, give me understanding for my life. Amen.

text: That their hearts might be comforted, being knit together in love, and unto all riches of the full assurance of understanding, to the acknowledgement of the mystery of God, and of the Father, and of Christ…
reflection: Paul longed for the believers in Colosse, many of whom he had never met. He prayed "That their hearts might be comforted, being knit together in love, and unto all riches of the full assurance of understanding." Notice how wisdom and love are woven together here. Paul wanted their hearts encouraged, their community knit together like threads in a strong fabric, and their understanding full and confident. True wisdom is not cold or isolated. It grows best in loving community. When we learn together, pray together, and encourage one another, our understanding of God deepens. We see aspects of His truth through each other's eyes. And the goal of it all is to know Christ, in whom the mystery of God is revealed. Today, think about the people you grow alongside. Thank God for them. If you have been trying to grow alone, consider reaching out to join others in studying God's Word. Hearts knit together in love become rich in understanding.
question: Who are the people you grow alongside in faith, and how can you thank God for them?
prayer: Lord, knit my heart together with others in love. Thank You for the people I grow with, and fill us with the full assurance of understanding. Amen.

text: Who is a wise man and endued with knowledge among you? let him shew out of a good conversation his works with meekness of wisdom.
reflection: James asks a direct question: "Who is a wise man and endued with knowledge among you?" Then he gives a practical answer: "let him shew out of a good conversation his works with meekness of wisdom." In the old English of the King James Bible, conversation means way of life. So James is saying that wisdom is proven not by what we know, but by how we live. And it is marked by meekness, a gentle humility. Real wisdom does not show off. It does not need to win every argument or prove how much it knows. Instead, it quietly does good, treats others with kindness, and lives with integrity. Many people talk wisely but live foolishly. James calls us to the opposite. Let your life speak louder than your words. Today, demonstrate wisdom through humble, good works. Help someone without drawing attention to yourself. Respond gently in a tense moment. That is what heavenly wisdom looks like in everyday life.
question: How can you show wisdom today through a humble, good deed that draws no attention to yourself?
prayer: Lord, let my wisdom be seen in how I live, not just in what I know. Give me the meekness of wisdom to serve quietly and respond gently today. Amen.

text: Here is wisdom. Let him that hath understanding count the number of the beast: for it is the number of a man; and his number is Six hundred threescore and six.
reflection: Revelation 13 describes a beast that opposes God and deceives the world. In the middle of this dark vision comes a call: "Here is wisdom. Let him that hath understanding count the number of the beast: for it is the number of a man." People have speculated about this number for centuries. But notice what the verse emphasizes. It is a call for wisdom and discernment. God's people need understanding to recognize evil for what it is, especially when it appears powerful and impressive. And the number, John says, is the number of a man. However frightening evil may look, it is limited. It is human, not divine. It cannot match the power of God. True wisdom does not get lost in fear or fascination with darkness. It sees clearly, stays faithful, and trusts that God reigns over all. Today, ask God for discernment to recognize what is false. And take courage. Every power that opposes God is limited and temporary.
question: What falsehood do you need discernment to recognize, and how does God's reign give you courage?
prayer: Lord, give me wisdom and discernment to recognize what is false. Keep me faithful, and remind me that every power opposed to You is limited and temporary. Amen.

text: To know wisdom and instruction; to perceive the words of understanding…
reflection: The book of Proverbs opens by explaining its purpose: "To know wisdom and instruction; to perceive the words of understanding." It was written so that we might become wise. Much of it is presented as a parent teaching a child, and just a few verses later the reader is urged not to forsake the teaching of a mother. On this Mother's Day, many of us remember the women who first taught us wisdom. Some taught with words, others by example, patience, and prayer. Not everyone has a mother who did this well, and that can make this day tender. But God often places nurturing people in our lives: grandmothers, aunts, teachers, mentors, and friends who have shared wisdom like a mother. Proverbs reminds us that wisdom is meant to be passed down with love. Today, thank God for those who instructed you with care. Reach out to one of them if you can. And ask God to help you share wisdom gently with the next generation.
question: Who first taught you wisdom, and how could you thank them today?
prayer: Lord, thank You for the mothers and mentors who taught me wisdom with love. Bless them today, and help me pass on wisdom gently to the next generation. Amen.

text: For if I pray in an unknown tongue, my spirit prayeth, but my understanding is unfruitful.
reflection: Paul was writing to a church that loved spiritual gifts, especially speaking in tongues. But he urged them to remember that understanding matters too: "For if I pray in an unknown tongue, my spirit prayeth, but my understanding is unfruitful." Paul was not dismissing heartfelt worship. He was saying that worship is fullest when both the spirit and the mind are engaged. In the following verse, he says he will pray with the spirit and with the understanding also. God does not ask us to switch off our minds when we come to Him. He wants all of us: heart, soul, and mind. Faith is not anti-intellectual, and it is not merely intellectual either. It engages the whole person. Today, as you pray or worship, be fully present. Think about the words you sing. Understand the prayers you pray. Let your mind and spirit work together. Worship that engages your understanding bears fruit in your life and in the lives of others.
question: How can you engage both your mind and your spirit in worship today?
prayer: Lord, I want to worship You with my spirit and with my understanding. Help me mean the words I sing and pray, and let my worship bear fruit. Amen.

text: And Moses was learned in all the wisdom of the Egyptians, and was mighty in words and in deeds.
reflection: Stephen described Moses this way: "And Moses was learned in all the wisdom of the Egyptians, and was mighty in words and in deeds." Raised in Pharaoh's palace, Moses had the best education in the world. He was capable, articulate, and influential. Yet when he tried to deliver Israel by his own strength, he failed and fled into the desert. It was only after forty years tending sheep in the wilderness that God called him. By then, Moses felt weak and unqualified. He even claimed he was not eloquent. But that was when God's strength could truly work through him. Our skills and training are gifts, and God can use them. But they are not enough on their own. The greatest strength comes when we depend on God rather than ourselves. Today, offer your abilities to God. And if you feel weak or unqualified, take heart. God often does His mightiest work through people who have learned to rely on Him.
question: What ability can you offer to God today, or what weakness can you trust Him to work through?
prayer: Lord, I offer You my abilities and my weaknesses. Teach me to depend on You and not on myself, and do Your mighty work through me. Amen.

text: Ever learning, and never able to come to the knowledge of the truth.
reflection: Paul describes a troubling kind of person: "Ever learning, and never able to come to the knowledge of the truth." These people were always collecting new ideas, always curious, always listening, yet never arriving at truth that changed their lives. Their learning was endless but fruitless. This is a warning for every age, especially our own. We have access to more information than any generation before us. We can listen to sermons, podcasts, and lectures all day long. Yet information alone does not make us wise. Learning must lead to truth, and truth must lead to transformation. Growing in wisdom means not only taking in knowledge but letting it change us. It means applying what we learn, obeying what we understand, and coming to know Jesus, who is the truth. Today, instead of seeking something new, take one truth you already know and put it into practice. Let your learning become living. That is how real growth happens.
question: What truth you already know could you put into practice today?
prayer: Lord, I do not want to be ever learning but never changed. Help me take one truth I already know and live it today, so my learning becomes living. Amen.

text: And when he saw a fig tree in the way, he came to it, and found nothing thereon, but leaves only, and said unto it, Let no fruit grow on thee henceforward for ever. And presently the fig tree withered away.
reflection: As Jesus walked toward Jerusalem, He saw a fig tree full of leaves. From a distance, it looked healthy and promising. But when He came close, He "found nothing thereon, but leaves only." So He spoke a word of judgment, and the tree withered. This was an acted parable. The tree represented religion that looks impressive on the outside but produces no real fruit. Jesus was about to enter a temple full of activity, but lacking true worship and justice. It is a sobering picture for us. We can have all the leaves of faith, church attendance, religious words, outward appearances, and still lack the fruit of love, obedience, and genuine trust. Jesus is not impressed by leaves. He looks for fruit. But here is the hope: He also gives us the life that produces fruit. When we stay connected to Him, real fruit grows. Today, ask Jesus to look closely at your life. Invite Him to grow genuine fruit where there have only been leaves.
question: Where in your life are there leaves without fruit, and how can you invite Jesus to look closely?
prayer: Lord Jesus, look closely at my life. Where there are only leaves, grow genuine fruit, and keep me connected to You, the source of real life. Amen.

text: But the wisdom that is from above is first pure, then peaceable, gentle, and easy to be intreated, full of mercy and good fruits, without partiality, and without hypocrisy.
reflection: James gives one of the most beautiful descriptions of wisdom in the Bible: "But the wisdom that is from above is first pure, then peaceable, gentle, and easy to be intreated, full of mercy and good fruits, without partiality, and without hypocrisy." Read that list slowly. Heavenly wisdom is pure, free from selfish motives. It is peaceable, seeking harmony rather than conflict. It is gentle, not harsh or forceful. It is easy to be intreated, meaning open to reason and willing to listen. It is full of mercy, overflowing with good deeds. It is impartial, treating everyone fairly. And it is sincere, without pretending. This is not the world's idea of wisdom, which often values cleverness, winning, and getting ahead. God's wisdom looks like the character of Jesus. Today, use this verse as a mirror. Which of these qualities do you see in your life? Which ones need to grow? Ask God for the wisdom that comes from above.
question: Which quality of heavenly wisdom, pure, peaceable, gentle, or merciful, most needs to grow in you?
prayer: Lord, give me the wisdom that is from above: pure, peaceable, gentle, open to reason, full of mercy and good fruits, without partiality or hypocrisy. Amen.

text: The fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom: a good understanding have all they that do his commandments: his praise endureth for ever.
reflection: Psalm 111 is a song of praise for God's great works, and it ends with this conclusion: "The fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom: a good understanding have all they that do his commandments." Notice the connection between understanding and obedience. Good understanding belongs to those who do His commandments. Wisdom is not only about what we know but about how we respond. When we put God's Word into practice, our understanding deepens. Obedience becomes a teacher. Many of us want understanding first, so that we can decide whether to obey. But God often works the other way around. As we trust Him enough to obey, He gives us understanding we could not have gained any other way. And the psalm ends with praise: "his praise endureth for ever." A wise life ultimately leads to worship. Today, take a step of obedience in something God has shown you. Trust that understanding will follow, and let your life become a song of praise.
question: What step of obedience is God asking of you, trusting that understanding will follow?
prayer: Lord, the fear of You is the beginning of wisdom. Help me do what You have shown me, deepen my understanding as I obey, and let my life become a song of praise. Amen.

text: An instructor of the foolish, a teacher of babes, which hast the form of knowledge and of the truth in the law.
reflection: Paul is speaking to someone who felt confident about their spiritual knowledge. They saw themselves as "An instructor of the foolish, a teacher of babes." They had the law, the form of knowledge and truth. But Paul goes on to ask a piercing question: you who teach others, do you not teach yourself? It is easy to know the right answers and still fail to live them. It is easy to correct others while ignoring our own need for correction. A teachable heart never outgrows the need to learn. On this Pentecost Sunday, we remember that the Holy Spirit came not to make believers feel superior, but to transform them from the inside out. True spiritual maturity is marked by humility. The more we know, the more aware we become of how much we still need God. Today, before you help someone else grow, ask God to search your own heart. Be a learner first. Let the Spirit teach you, and then share what you have learned with grace.
question: Before you help someone else grow, what does God want to teach you first?
prayer: Lord, search my heart before I correct anyone else. Make me a learner first, teach me by Your Spirit, and help me share what I learn with grace. Amen.

text: And wisdom and knowledge shall be the stability of thy times, and strength of salvation: the fear of the LORD is his treasure.
reflection: In a time of national crisis, Isaiah gave a promise of security: "And wisdom and knowledge shall be the stability of thy times, and strength of salvation: the fear of the LORD is his treasure." When everything around us is changing, what keeps us steady? Isaiah says wisdom and knowledge from God bring stability. They are like an anchor in shifting seas. Our times may be uncertain. Economies rise and fall, health changes, and relationships go through seasons. But God's wisdom gives us solid footing. It helps us respond calmly rather than react in fear. And notice the final phrase: the fear of the LORD is his treasure. Reverence for God is not a burden; it is a treasure. It is the most valuable thing we can have, because it connects us to the One who never changes. Today, if your times feel unstable, anchor yourself in God's wisdom. Treasure your relationship with Him above all else. He will be your stability and strength.
question: What feels unstable in your life right now, and how can God's wisdom be your anchor?
prayer: Lord, You are the stability of my times. When everything shifts around me, anchor me in Your wisdom, and let reverence for You be my treasure. Amen.

text: Buy the truth, and sell it not; also wisdom, and instruction, and understanding.
reflection: Proverbs gives some unusual shopping advice: "Buy the truth, and sell it not; also wisdom, and instruction, and understanding." The picture is of a merchant who finds something so valuable that he is willing to pay whatever it costs. But once he has it, he refuses to sell it at any price. Truth and wisdom are worth acquiring, even when they cost us something. Sometimes the cost is time spent studying and praying. Sometimes it is pride, when we have to admit we were wrong. Sometimes it is comfort, when truth challenges our habits or opinions. But once we have found truth, we must hold on to it. There will be pressures to trade it away for popularity, convenience, or gain. The world offers many deals that require compromising what we know is right. Proverbs says: do not sell. Today, value truth more than approval. Invest in wisdom, and refuse to trade it away for anything less.
question: Where are you tempted to trade truth for approval or convenience?
prayer: Lord, help me buy the truth and never sell it. Give me courage to value truth more than approval, and to hold on to wisdom whatever it costs. Amen.

text: For to one is given by the Spirit the word of wisdom; to another the word of knowledge by the same Spirit…
reflection: Paul describes the many gifts the Holy Spirit gives to the church. He begins with these: "For to one is given by the Spirit the word of wisdom; to another the word of knowledge by the same Spirit." Notice that the gifts are given to different people. No one has all of them. One person may have a gift for wise counsel, another for understanding and explaining truth. These gifts are not meant to make anyone feel superior. They are given for the good of the whole community. We need each other. The wise counselor needs the teacher, and the teacher needs the encourager. Everyone has something to contribute, and everyone has something to receive. In this season after Pentecost, remember that the Spirit has given you gifts too. Perhaps you do not see them clearly yet. Ask God to show you how He has equipped you. And thank Him for the people whose gifts have helped you grow in wisdom and understanding.
question: How has God equipped you to help others, and whose gifts have helped you grow?
prayer: Holy Spirit, thank You for the gifts You give to Your church. Show me how You have equipped me, and help me use my gifts for the good of others. Amen.

text: Now when they saw the boldness of Peter and John, and perceived that they were unlearned and ignorant men, they marvelled; and they took knowledge of them, that they had been with Jesus.
reflection: Peter and John had just been arrested for healing a man and preaching about Jesus. When they stood before the religious council, they spoke with remarkable confidence. The leaders were astonished. These were ordinary fishermen, not trained scholars. Then the leaders realized something: "they took knowledge of them, that they had been with Jesus." That was the explanation. Their boldness and wisdom did not come from schools or titles. It came from time spent with Jesus. The same is true for us. You do not need impressive credentials to make an impact for God. What changes a life is time with Jesus. In prayer, in His Word, in fellowship with Him, we are shaped to reflect His character. And people notice. Today, spend unhurried time with Jesus. Let His presence shape your words and actions. Then go into your day in a way that makes others wonder, and perhaps realize, that you have been with Him.
question: How can you spend unhurried time with Jesus today so that your life shows you have been with Him?
prayer: Lord Jesus, I want to be with You. Let time in Your presence shape my words and actions, so that others can tell I have been with You. Amen.

text: In whom are hid all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge.
reflection: Paul makes a breathtaking claim about Jesus: "In whom are hid all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge." All of them. Not some, not most, but all. Every true insight, every genuine understanding, every deep wisdom finds its source in Christ. The word hid suggests treasure buried in a field, waiting to be discovered. It does not mean the treasure is kept from us. It means it is stored up in Christ and revealed to those who seek Him. Paul wrote this because some people in Colosse were being drawn to complicated philosophies that promised secret knowledge. Paul's answer was simple: you do not need to look elsewhere. Everything you need is in Jesus. Many people today search far and wide for wisdom. They try new ideas, new teachers, new paths. But the richest treasure is found in knowing Christ. Today, go deeper in Him. Read the Gospels. Learn His words. Every treasure of wisdom is waiting to be discovered there.
question: Where have you been searching for wisdom outside of Christ?
prayer: Lord Jesus, in You are hidden all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge. Draw me deeper into You, and let me discover Your riches in Your Word. Amen.

text: For if after they have escaped the pollutions of the world through the knowledge of the Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ, they are again entangled therein, and overcome, the latter end is worse with them than the beginning.
reflection: Peter gives a sobering warning: "if after they have escaped the pollutions of the world through the knowledge of the Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ, they are again entangled therein, and overcome, the latter end is worse with them than the beginning." He is describing people who once experienced the freedom that comes through knowing Jesus, but later drifted back into the very things that had enslaved them. It is a reminder that spiritual drift is real. Old habits, old temptations, and old ways of thinking can creep back in slowly, until we find ourselves tangled again. But notice how the escape happened in the first place: through knowing Jesus our Savior. The same remedy remains. If you feel yourself drifting, the answer is not despair but returning to Him. Stay close to the One who set you free. Guard your heart. Keep knowing Him. Today, if any old entanglement is pulling at you, run to Jesus, the Savior who still frees.
question: Is there an old entanglement pulling at you that you need to run from to Jesus?
prayer: Lord Jesus, You set me free. Guard my heart from drifting back into what once enslaved me, and when I am pulled away, help me run to You. Amen.

text: Yea doubtless, and I count all things but loss for the excellency of the knowledge of Christ Jesus my Lord: for whom I have suffered the loss of all things, and do count them but dung, that I may win Christ…
reflection: Paul had every reason to be proud of his background and achievements. But after meeting Jesus, everything changed. He wrote, "I count all things but loss for the excellency of the knowledge of Christ Jesus my Lord." He even used a harsh word to describe his former achievements, comparing them to refuse thrown away. Why? Not because they were worthless in themselves, but because knowing Jesus was so much greater. Compared to Him, everything else faded. That is how precious Christ is. Knowing Him personally is more valuable than wealth, status, success, or reputation. Paul lost much for following Jesus, yet he considered it a bargain. Today, consider what you value most. What would you be most afraid to lose? Bring those things before God. Ask Him to help you treasure Jesus above all. Nothing else will satisfy your soul like knowing Him. He is the greatest treasure, and He is worth everything.
question: What are you most afraid to lose, and can you treasure Jesus above it?
prayer: Lord Jesus, knowing You is worth more than anything I could gain or lose. Help me hold all things loosely and treasure You above all. Amen.

text: And we know that the Son of God is come, and hath given us an understanding, that we may know him that is true, and we are in him that is true, even in his Son Jesus Christ. This is the true God, and eternal life.
reflection: John closes his first letter with a statement of certainty: "And we know that the Son of God is come, and hath given us an understanding, that we may know him that is true." John was not uncertain about the most important things. Jesus has come. He has given us understanding. And through Him, we can know the true God. In a world full of confusion, competing claims, and uncertainty, this verse offers solid ground. We do not have to guess who God is. Jesus has revealed Him. And we are not merely spectators of truth; John says "we are in him that is true, even in his Son Jesus Christ." We are united with the One who is truth itself. Wisdom, in the end, is not a philosophy. It is a Person. Today, rest in the certainty that Jesus gives. When doubts arise, return to what you know. The Son of God has come. You can know the true God through Him.
question: When doubts arise, what do you know for certain about Jesus?
prayer: Lord Jesus, Son of God, You have come and given me understanding to know the true God. When doubts arise, bring me back to what I know in You. Amen.

text: And Jesus answered and said unto it, No man eat fruit of thee hereafter for ever. And his disciples heard it.
reflection: Mark records the moment Jesus spoke to the fig tree that had leaves but no fruit: "No man eat fruit of thee hereafter for ever. And his disciples heard it." That last phrase is worth noticing. The disciples heard it. Jesus wanted them to learn from this moment. The next day, when they passed the withered tree, Jesus taught them about faith and prayer. A barren tree became a lesson in fruitfulness. God desires fruit in our lives: love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, faithfulness. Not just the appearance of spiritual life, but its real evidence. And how does fruit grow? Through faith in God, through prayer, and through staying connected to Jesus. Fruitfulness is not achieved by straining. It grows naturally when we abide in Him. Today, listen like the disciples did. Ask Jesus what He wants to teach you about fruitfulness. Where does your faith need to grow deeper roots? Stay connected to Him, and let real fruit grow.
question: Where does your faith need to grow deeper roots to bear real fruit?
prayer: Lord Jesus, teach me what You want me to learn about fruitfulness. Deepen my roots in You, and let real fruit grow in my life. Amen.

text: Give instruction to a wise man, and he will be yet wiser: teach a just man, and he will increase in learning.
reflection: Here is a simple test of wisdom: how do you respond to instruction? Proverbs says, "Give instruction to a wise man, and he will be yet wiser: teach a just man, and he will increase in learning." Wise people are not those who already know everything. They are the ones who keep learning. When corrected, they listen. When taught, they grow. In contrast, the proud person resists instruction and stays stuck. One of the signs of spiritual maturity is a teachable spirit. It welcomes feedback, considers correction, and is willing to change. That is not always easy. Our pride can bristle when someone points out a blind spot. But a teachable heart sees instruction as a gift, an opportunity to become wiser. Today, notice how you respond to correction or advice. Instead of defending yourself, consider what you might learn. Ask God to give you a heart that welcomes instruction. The wise become wiser because they never stop learning.
question: How do you usually respond to correction, and what might you learn from it this time?
prayer: Lord, give me a heart that welcomes instruction. When I am corrected, help me listen instead of defending myself, so I may grow wiser. Amen.

text: And Jesus increased in wisdom and stature, and in favour with God and man.
reflection: We know very little about the childhood of Jesus, but Luke gives us one beautiful summary: "And Jesus increased in wisdom and stature, and in favour with God and man." Jesus grew. He grew in wisdom, in His mind and understanding. He grew in stature, in His body. He grew in favor with God, in His spiritual life. And He grew in favor with people, in His relationships. This is a picture of healthy, balanced growth. It reminds us that growth is a normal and good part of life. Even the Son of God, in His humanity, went through a process of growing up. We should not be discouraged that we are still growing. God is patient with the process. And this verse invites us to grow in every area: mind, body, spirit, and relationships. Today, consider which area of your life needs attention. Take one small step to grow there. Just as Jesus grew, you can grow too.
question: Which area of your life, mind, body, spirit, or relationships, most needs to grow right now?
prayer: Lord Jesus, You grew in wisdom and stature and in favor with God and people. Help me grow in every area of my life, one small step at a time. Amen.

text: As also ye have acknowledged us in part, that we are your rejoicing, even as ye also are ours in the day of the Lord Jesus.
reflection: Paul shares a tender hope with the Corinthians. He writes that "we are your rejoicing, even as ye also are ours in the day of the Lord Jesus." Despite tension and misunderstanding between them, Paul looked forward to a day when they would rejoice in each other before Christ. On that day, Paul would rejoice over the Corinthians as evidence of God's work, and they would rejoice over Paul as the one who brought them the gospel. This is a beautiful way to view our relationships. The people God has placed in our lives are not just companions for now. They are part of our eternal joy. One day, in the presence of Jesus, we will see how God used us in each other's lives. Today, think of someone who has helped you grow in faith. Thank God for them. And think of someone you are investing in. Remember that your faithfulness to them will be a cause for joy on the day of the Lord Jesus.
question: Who has helped you grow in faith, and whom are you investing in?
prayer: Lord, thank You for those who brought me Your truth. Make me faithful to the people I am investing in, so we may rejoice together on the day of the Lord Jesus. Amen.

text: Which things also we speak, not in the words which man's wisdom teacheth, but which the Holy Ghost teacheth; comparing spiritual things with spiritual.
reflection: Paul explains where his message came from: "Which things also we speak, not in the words which man's wisdom teacheth, but which the Holy Ghost teacheth." Paul was well educated and could have impressed people with clever speeches. But he chose to rely on the Spirit's wisdom rather than human eloquence. The gospel is not a product of human genius. It is revealed truth, taught by God's Spirit. This means that spiritual understanding is not limited to the brilliant or the highly trained. The Holy Spirit is the teacher, and He teaches anyone who is willing to learn. When you read Scripture, you are not alone. The same Spirit who inspired the words is present to help you understand them. Today, as you read God's Word, invite the Holy Spirit to be your teacher. Ask Him to open your eyes to see what He wants to show you. Rely on His wisdom, not just your own. He delights to teach those who ask.
question: How can you invite the Holy Spirit to be your teacher as you read God's Word today?
prayer: Holy Spirit, be my teacher. Open my eyes as I read Your Word, and help me rely on Your wisdom rather than my own. Amen.

text: Teach me good judgment and knowledge: for I have believed thy commandments.
reflection: Psalm 119 is a long love song about God's Word, and in this verse the psalmist prays, "Teach me good judgment and knowledge: for I have believed thy commandments." Notice the reason he gives. He wants to learn because he already believes. Faith creates hunger for understanding. When we trust God's Word, we want to know it better and live it more wisely. Good judgment is the ability to apply knowledge rightly in real situations. It is one thing to know a command; it is another to know how to live it wisely in a complicated world. That is why we need God to teach us. This prayer is perfect for anyone who wants to grow. It is humble, recognizing our need. It is hopeful, trusting God to teach. And it is rooted in faith. Today, pray this verse as your own. Ask God for good judgment in the decisions before you. Believe His Word, and let Him teach you how to live it.
question: What decision in front of you needs good judgment from God?
prayer: Lord, teach me good judgment and knowledge, for I believe Your commandments. Help me apply Your Word wisely in the decisions before me today. Amen.

text: They also that erred in spirit shall come to understanding, and they that murmured shall learn doctrine.
reflection: Isaiah offers a hopeful promise for those who have gone astray: "They also that erred in spirit shall come to understanding, and they that murmured shall learn doctrine." Those who wandered will come to understanding. Those who grumbled and complained will learn the truth. This is a beautiful picture of God's patience and grace. He does not give up on people who make mistakes or who resist Him for a while. He continues to work, to teach, and to draw them back. Perhaps you have erred in spirit. Maybe you have complained against God or drifted from His ways. This verse says there is hope. God can still bring you to understanding. Or maybe you are praying for someone who has wandered. Do not lose heart. God is able to open their eyes. As we close this month of wisdom and growth, give thanks that God is a patient teacher. He keeps teaching us, even when we have been slow to learn.
question: Who has wandered or been slow to learn that you can keep praying for, including yourself?
prayer: Lord, You are a patient teacher. Thank You for not giving up on those who wander. Open the eyes of the ones I pray for, and keep teaching me too. Amen.
